claims.text: Each month's interest on each debt is balance times yearly rate divided by 12, rounded half up to the cent.
Months to debt-free for each plan is counted month by month, exactly.
Total interest for each plan is the sum of every month's interest, to the cent.
The order of payoff lists each debt with the month it reaches zero.
When a debt is paid off, its smallest payment rolls into the next debt in line.
The difference shows how many months and how many dollars of interest the two plans are apart.
If a smallest payment does not cover the first month's interest, the tool says so plainly and works out nothing.
A plan that would pass 1,200 months stops with a plain message instead of looping.
Messy typing never gives a wrong number, NaN or a crash.
A bad entry gets a calm message in plain words that names the debt and the field.
